headline: Trump teleprompter aide made $100,000 betting on presidential speeches, reports say
summary: Gabriel Perez, a White House teleprompter operator, is on leave after allegedly winning over $100,000 on Kalshi by betting on the length of President Trump's speeches.
details: Gabriel Perez, President Donald Trump's teleprompter operator, has been placed on administrative leave after reportedly betting on dozens of the President's speeches on the platform Kalshi. He allegedly made more than $100,000 by betting on the length of speeches, including the State of the Union address and remarks at the World Economic Forum.

Perez reportedly had the final eyes on nearly all of the president's prepared remarks, which likely provided an advantage for informed bets. He also reportedly backed out of certain bets when Trump went off script, further indicating insider knowledge.

Kalshi promptly flagged and referred these trades to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), the body overseeing such platforms. Perez has reportedly confessed to some of the trades in an interview with investigators, and the CFTC is willing to settle if he returns his winnings.

White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt confirmed Perez's unpaid administrative leave, calling his actions "deeply unfortunate" and a "disgrace." She added that Perez "will no longer be here" in his role.

In April 2026, Kalshi introduced new policies to prevent politicians and athletes from betting on their own elections or games, later suspending three political candidates for violations. Further restrictions in June required users to disclose their employment before placing certain bets. Attempts to regulate prediction markets have faced challenges, with a US Circuit Court of Appeals ruling against New Jersey's ban on Kalshi, placing regulatory power firmly with the CFTC.
caption:
A White House teleprompter operator allegedly made over $100,000 by betting on President Trump's speeches. He's now on administrative leave after Kalshi flagged his trades.

Gabriel Perez, President Donald Trump's teleprompter operator, has been placed on administrative leave after reportedly betting on dozens of the President's speeches on the platform Kalshi. He allegedly made more than $100,000 by betting on the length of speeches, including the State of the Union address and remarks at the World Economic Forum.

Perez reportedly had the final eyes on nearly all of the president's prepared remarks, which likely provided an advantage for informed bets. He also reportedly backed out of certain bets when Trump went off script, further indicating insider knowledge.

Kalshi promptly flagged and referred these trades to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), the body overseeing such platforms. Perez has reportedly confessed to some of the trades in an interview with investigators, and the CFTC is willing to settle if he returns his winnings.

White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt confirmed Perez's unpaid administrative leave, calling his actions "deeply unfortunate" and a "disgrace." She added that Perez "will no longer be here" in his role.

In April 2026, Kalshi introduced new policies to prevent politicians and athletes from betting on their own elections or games, later suspending three political candidates for violations. Further restrictions in June required users to disclose their employment before placing certain bets. Attempts to regulate prediction markets have faced challenges, with a US Circuit Court of Appeals ruling against New Jersey's ban on Kalshi, placing regulatory power firmly with the CFTC.
